title: scale-controller + rate-limiter interaction causing reserved-capacity undershoot
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (mid-market SLA tier) experienced sustained request queuing and 429/503 errors during a regional traffic spike on 2026-02-28. Root cause analysis indicates the dedicated scale controller incorrectly inferred available headroom because its telemetry ingest was being throttled by the internal rate-limiter, producing artificially low request metrics. The autoscaler reacted by shrinking reserved pools and failing to honor burst allocations, causing capacity shortfall for reserved tenants.

Impact: High. Affected customers saw degraded latency and failed bursts for ~45 minutes during peak. Immediate mitigation (fallback routing to hosted model variants) partially reduced error surface but increased cost and exposed tenants to cross-tenant routing fallback.

What went wrong (high level):
- The scale controller computes headroom using a sliding-window of per-tenant request/slot allocations and a telemetry-derived burst signal.
- When the internal rate-limiter (protecting the telemetry ingestion path) reached its soft threshold under high cardinality telemetry, it started dropping telemetry points for a subset of tenants.
- Missing telemetry was treated as zero traffic rather than unknown, causing the headroom estimator to undercount demand.
- Autoscaler aggressively condensed reserved pools to the computed need, and the burst protector failed to trigger because it relies on the same telemetry signal.

Reproduction steps:
1) Run synthetic driver producing high-cardinality short-burst traffic across 40 tenants in a region.
2) Configure telemetry rate-limiter to current prod parameters (see runbook link).
3) Observe telemetry drop and autoscaler downscales reserved pools below expected burst capacity.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back recent scale-controller change that tightened the telemetry interpretation rules (hotfix commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812).
- Enabled conservative minimum headroom policy for all reserved pools in the affected region (console flag set at 2026-03-01T05:30Z).
- Routed high-priority tenants to a fallback hosted path where policy permits (support docs and comms sent).

Proposed permanent fix (multi-pronged):
1) Treat missing telemetry as "unknown" instead of zero. Add a telemetry health heartbeat metric and require N successful scrapes before allowing aggressive downscales (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=98765432).
2) Introduce a rate-limiter admission control shim for the telemetry pipeline that returns explicit backpressure signals to the scale controller so it can use a conservative fallback rather than assuming zero traffic.
3) Add a hysteresis window and minimum-viable-headroom config per reserved-pool; default to 15% headroom or 2 GPU-equivalents (whichever is larger) for tenants with SLA >= tier-2.
4) Extend the burst-protector to use request path observability (trace-based sampling) as a secondary signal if metrics are missing.

Planned rollout:
- Phase 1 (canary): Implement telemetry-heartbeat + unknown-as-default. Roll to 2 test regions behind feature flag (runtime-1.21-canary). Monitor for 48h.
- Phase 2: Rate-limiter shim + hysteresis defaults. Gradual rollout with ops guardrails and kill-switch.
- Phase 3: Extend burst-protector and post-deploy retrofitting of reserved pools.

Monitoring and KPIs:
- New telemetry_heartbeat{region,pool} metric; alert if >1 scrape missing in 2m window.
- Headroom_estimate_delta exposing last-known-raw vs adjusted estimate.
- Customer-facing SLO: 99.5% request success for reserved-pool tenants during bursts; flag regressions to SRE and account teams.

Stakeholders and comms:
- Engineering owners: Luis Ortega (assignee), Priya Nair (runtime), Tomasz Zielinski (observability).
- Customer success & account leads notified: Sarah Patel, Omar Haddad.
- Legal/compliance: looped in for customers on private deployments.

Follow-ups (postmortem actions):
- Update reserved-pool runbook to include telemetry-health gating (owners: SRE).
- Backfill missing telemetry for the incident window and recompute billing impact (billing team).
- Customer postmortem and credits discussion for affected tenants.

References and artifacts: see links below for PRs, dashboards, and incident chat logs.
